name: John Wesley
title: John Wesley: Aldersgate and trust in the grace of Christ
description: John Wesley’s experience at Aldersgate on May 24, 1738, read through Methodist memory, and what it means to trust in Christ.

sections.heading: A meeting in London
paragraphs: On May 24, 1738, John Wesley attended a Christian meeting in the Aldersgate area of London. Methodist memory keeps that night as a decisive moment in his life. He was already a man devoted to religious practice; the event is remembered for the change he described in his personal trust in Christ.

The explanation from United Methodist Communications points to the entry in his journal. Wesley heard a reading of Martin Luther’s preface to Romans and told of a new assurance concerning grace and salvation. The testimony belongs to his own experience and should be presented as such, without turning his personal language into a required formula for others.

sections.heading: Remembering the beginning without reducing everything to a moment
paragraphs: The Methodist Church commemorates the event on Wesley Day and Aldersgate Sunday. That remembrance shows the place experience holds in the tradition that grew up around Wesley. It also helps distinguish between a historical date and the interpretation a Christian community gives to it.

The Aldersgate account sets before the reader a person who was seeking spiritual assurance despite his religious devotion. The Methodist source stresses that John and Charles were already devout before May 1738. A careful biography can recognize the depth of the change without presenting the earlier years as a life lacking all faith or service.

reflection: Ephesians 2:8–10 joins salvation by grace with a life directed toward good works. That connection lets us reflect on the difference between resting in Christ and seeking security in our own religious effort. Service has value, but the believer’s hope rests on the grace of God.

Wesley’s story can encourage those who know Christian practices and still struggle with fear or insecurity. It also teaches prudence in listening to testimonies: people express their faith with different words and experiences. The church can help people read the Scriptures and walk with them as they grow, without requiring everyone to repeat the same emotional experience.
review_note: The spiritual experience is identified as testimony. Wesley’s method or experience is not made into a universal doctrinal rule.
source_labels: The Methodist Church. “Aldersgate Sunday,” explanation of the Wesley Day commemoration.
